stem.text: The depth of snow on a field, measured in inches, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function D of time t, measured in hours. It is known that \( D'(5) = 3.5 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( D'(5) = 3.5 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 5 hours, the depth of snow on the field is increasing at a rate of 3.5 inches per hour.

worked_solution.text: \( D'(5) \) is the rate of change of the depth of snow on the field at the instant t = 5, so it is measured in inches per hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: derivative as a rate of change

worked_solution.text: The value is positive, so the depth of snow on the field is increasing at that instant, by 3.5 inches for each hour.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction

options.label: At time t = 5 hours, the depth of snow on the field is increasing at a rate of 3.5 hours per inch.
options.derivation: the units assembled the wrong way round, time units over quantity units

options.label: At time t = 5 hours, the depth of snow on the field has changed by a total of 3.5 inches.
options.derivation: the derivative value read as an amount, the total change in the quantity, rather than a rate

options.label: Over the first 5 hours, the depth of snow on the field is increasing at a rate of 3.5 inches per hour.
options.derivation: the instant replaced by the whole interval up to it, so the interpretation no longer says when the rate holds

options.label: At time t = 5 hours, the depth of snow on the field is increasing at a rate of 3.5 inches per hour.
